corinthians1.7.p1.b1.text: Now for the matters you wrote about: It is good to abstain from sexual relations.

corinthians1.7.p1.b2.text: But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.

corinthians1.7.p2.b3.text: The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.

corinthians1.7.p2.b4.text: I say this as a concession, not as a command.

corinthians1.7.p2.b5.text: I wish that all men were as I am. But each man has his own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that.

corinthians1.7.p3.b6.text: Now to the unmarried and widows I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am.

corinthians1.7.p3.b7.text: … (not I, but the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.

corinthians1.7.p3.b8.text: But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.

corinthians1.7.p4.b9.text: To the rest I say this (I, not the Lord): If a brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.

corinthians1.7.p4.b10.text: … Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

corinthians1.7.p4.b11.text: … God has called you to live in peace.

corinthians1.7.p4.b12.text: How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband?

corinthians1.7.p5.b13.text: Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.

corinthians1.7.p5.b14.text: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.

corinthians1.7.p5.b15.text: Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.

corinthians1.7.p6.b16.text: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you—but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.

corinthians1.7.p6.b17.text: For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.

corinthians1.7.p6.b18.text: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.

corinthians1.7.p7.b19.text: Now about virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.

corinthians1.7.p7.b20.text: Because of the present crisis, I think it is good for a man to remain as he is.

corinthians1.7.p7.b21.text: But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. … I want to spare you this.

corinthians1.7.p8.b22.text: What I am saying, brothers, is that the time is short.

corinthians1.7.p8.b23.text: those who weep, as if they did not; those who are joyful, as if they were not;

corinthians1.7.p8.b24.text: those who make a purchase, as if they had nothing;

corinthians1.7.p8.b25.text: For this world in its present form is passing away.

corinthians1.7.p9.b26.text: I want you to be free from concern.

corinthians1.7.p9.b27.text: The unmarried man is concerned about the work of the Lord, how he can please the Lord.

corinthians1.7.p9.b28.text: But the married man is concerned about the affairs of this world, how he can please his wife,

corinthians1.7.p9.b29.text: I am saying this for your own good, … to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord.

corinthians1.7.p10.b30.text: So then, he who marries the virgin does well, but he who does not marry her does even better.

corinthians1.7.p10.b31.text: But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.

corinthians1.7.p10.b32.text: In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
